task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! My mobile data has been acting up — it either stops working completely or crawls along really slowly. I'd really like to get it sorted out today.

turns.thought:

- **Your phone number** (the line having the issue), or
- **Your full name and date of birth**

so I can pull up your account details.
turns.execution_output: User: Sure thing! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

Can you confirm which line is having the mobile data issue — is it the one ending in **555-123-2002**, or a different number on your account?

Let me check the details of that first line while you confirm.

I've found your account. Let me confirm a few details and then run a diagnostic on your device.

**Line with issue:** 555-123-2002 (Line L1002) — Premium Plan, 15 GB monthly limit
**Current usage:** 15.1 GB used of 15 GB — **you've exceeded your data limit**, which is why data has stopped or is crawling.

Before I fix it, could you run a quick speed test on your phone to confirm the current data state?

I've found the issue. Let me tell you what I found:

**Line:** 555-123-2002 (Line L1002) — Status: Active, Premium Plan (15 GB/month)
**Data used this cycle:** 15.1 GB out of a **15.0 GB limit**
**Billing cycle ends:** 2025-02-28

You've gone over your plan's monthly data allowance, which is why your data connection has been dropping out or crawling along. Your other lines look fine — line 555-123-2001 is Active with only 3.2 GB used.

There are two options to get you back up and running today:

**Option 1 — Refuel data:** Add extra data to this line right now. Your plan's rate is **$2.00 per GB**, and you can add up to **2 GB** (so $2.00 for 1 GB, or $4.00 for 2 GB). This applies immediately to the current cycle.

**Option 2 — Change plan:** Move to a plan with a higher data limit.

How would you like to proceed — and if you'd like to refuel, how many GB would you like to add (1 or 2)?
turns.execution_output: User: Ah, that makes sense — I had no idea I'd gone over. I definitely don't want to change my plan, so let's go with the refuel option. Please add the full 2 GB.

- You're close to your limit each month, so if this keeps happening, changing to a plan with more data could save you money — just let me know if you'd ever like to look into that.

turns.execution_output: User: Got it, thanks for adding that. Let me restart my phone now.

turns.thought: Let me check your device status to confirm what's going on.
Let me try to access your device's settings directly to check and correct this.

I wasn't able to run the remote device diagnostic tools on my end just now, but no worries — these are all settings you can change directly on your phone, and I'll walk you through it step by step.

**1. Turn off Airplane Mode (highest priority)**

This disables all wireless radios including cellular, and it would fully explain why your data isn't working at all:

- **Quickest way:** Swipe down from the top of your screen (twice, to open the full quick settings panel) and tap the **✈️ Airplane** icon so it turns gray/off.
- **Or via Settings:** Settings → **Network & Internet** → **Airplane mode** → toggle it **Off**.

After that, you should see signal bars (e.g. 5G/LTE with 📶) reappear in the status bar within a few seconds.

**2. Then confirm mobile data is on**

- Settings → **Network & Internet** → **Mobile network** → make sure **Mobile data** is toggled **On**.
- Also check that **Data Saver** is **Off** (Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver), since that can throttle speeds.

**3. About the VPN**

A VPN is connected, and VPNs can slow your connection down significantly, so if things are still crawling after step 1 and 2, please disconnect it as a test:

- Settings → **Network & Internet** → **VPN** → tap the connected VPN and select **Disconnect**.

Then try browsing again to compare.

**4. Battery at 80%** — that's perfectly normal, nothing to worry about there.

Once you've turned off Airplane Mode, please let me know what the status bar shows now (signal bars and whether the ✈️ icon is gone), and whether your data is working at normal speed. If it's still not right, I'll keep troubleshooting with you or get you over to our technical support team.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me turn off Airplane Mode first.

turns.thought: Good progress — Airplane Mode is off and you're getting a signal now. Let me try the remote tools again, since I can possibly apply these changes for you.

You're right — there are still three separate things keeping your data from working. Each one has a fix you can do right on the phone. The remote device tools aren't responding on my end, so I'll walk you through them and you can make the changes directly:

**1. Turn Mobile Data back ON**

Your status bar shows "📵 Data Disabled," which on its own would fully block mobile data.

- Open **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network**
- Toggle **Mobile data** to **On**

**2. Change off 2G to 4G/5G**

You're on 2G, which is an older network technology that can't deliver normal data speeds (and is too slow for picture messaging too). This is likely the cause of the "crawling" speed when it did connect.

- On that same **Mobile network** screen, tap **Preferred network mode** (sometimes called "Network mode")
- Select **5G/4G/3G auto** or **4G (LTE) preferred** — anything that includes 4G/5G rather than 2G-only

**3. Disconnect the VPN**

A connected VPN can slow mobile data dramatically, so it's worth removing as a variable while we test.

- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN**
- Tap the gear/settings icon next to the connected VPN, then tap **Disconnect**

**4. Reboot once more**

After making those three changes, restart your phone again so everything re-registers on the network.

Once it's back up, please tell me what your status bar shows. What I'd hope to see is something like "📶³ 5G" or "📶³ LTE" with "📱 Data Enabled" and no VPN icon.

One note on the poor signal: after switching off 2G, give it a moment to re-register — if you're in a basement or a building with thick walls, moving near a window or stepping outside can help. If the signal is still poor after all this, that points to something on our end (network coverage or the line itself) and I'll get you transferred to our technical support team to dig into it.

Go ahead and try those steps and let me know how it looks.
turns.execution_output: User: That's a lot of steps at once — I'd rather do them one at a time so I can tell you exactly what changes after each one. Which one should I do first?

turns.thought:
Absolutely — that's a smart approach. Let's do them one at a time.

**First: turn Mobile Data back ON.**

- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Network & Internet**
- Tap **Mobile network** (on some phones it's "SIMs" or "Mobile networks")
- Toggle **Mobile data** to **On**

That's it for now — leave the network mode and VPN alone for the moment.

Once you've done that, check your status bar and tell me what it shows. I'm specifically looking for whether the "📵 Data Disabled" message has changed to "📱 Data Enabled," and whether the speed or connectivity improved at all — even if it's still on 2G with poor signal, tell me exactly what you see. Then we'll move on to the next single step.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, turning mobile data on now.

turns.thought:
Good progress — Data Enabled is confirmed. Next single step:

**Turn OFF Data Saver.**

You're now seeing the "🔽 Data Saver" icon. Data Saver restricts background data usage and can make apps and browsing feel slow or unresponsive, so it's worth turning off while we sort this out.

- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Network & Internet**
- Tap **Data Saver**
- Toggle it **Off**

Just that one change for now — leave the 2G setting and the VPN as they are.

When it's done, check the status bar again and tell me what you see. I'm looking for whether the 🔽 Data Saver icon is gone, and whether speeds improved at all. Then we'll take the next single step.
turns.execution_output: User: Turning off Data Saver now.

turns.thought:
Data Saver icon is gone — good, that's cleared. Next single step:

**Switch your preferred network mode off 2G and onto 4G/5G.**

Being locked on 2G is very likely the reason things feel like they're crawling — 2G is an older network technology that can't deliver normal data speeds. Switching to a mode that includes 4G/5G should help both your speed and the signal your phone latches onto.

- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Network & Internet**
- Tap **Mobile network** (or "SIMs" / "Mobile networks")
- Tap **Preferred network mode** (sometimes called "Network mode")
- Select **5G/4G/3G auto** (or **4G (LTE) preferred**) — anything that includes 4G or 5G rather than 2G-only

That's the only change for this step — leave the VPN alone for now and don't reboot yet.

After you select it, wait a few seconds for the phone to re-register on the network, then check the status bar and tell me what it shows. I'm looking to see whether "2G" has changed to "4G"/"5G"/"LTE," and whether the signal bars have improved from 📶¹. Then we'll decide on the final VPN step.
turns.execution_output: User: Switching the network mode now.

turns.thought:
Great — that was the breakthrough. 📶⁴ Excellent on 5G with Data Enabled is exactly what we wanted to see.

On the VPN: you don't need to disconnect it urgently. A VPN is only a known cause of slowdowns when your connection is performing poorly — and right now your signal and network type look strong. So for this step, I'd suggest:

**Test your data first, with the VPN still on.** Open a browser and load a page, or play a short video, and see how it actually feels.

Then:

- **If it's fast and fine** — you're all set. No need to touch the VPN at all. Your original problem was the 2G network mode plus Mobile Data being disabled and Data Saver on, and all three are now resolved.
- **If it's still sluggish** despite the excellent 5G signal — that's when the VPN becomes the likely culprit. Disconnect it as a test: **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN →** tap the connected VPN → **Disconnect**. Then retest.

One thing worth keeping in mind: keeping the VPN on is your choice — it may be there for work or privacy reasons, and it doesn't need to stay off permanently. It's purely a troubleshooting step.

Also, just so you know, your **2 GB data refuel** from earlier is on the line and your cycle resets on **2025-02-28**.

Go ahead and test it, and let me know how the speed feels. If it's slow even on 5G with the VPN off, I'll get you over to our technical support team to dig deeper.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me run a speed test to see how it's actually performing.

turns.thought:
That's a strange one — your status bar looks perfect, yet the speed test reports no connection. That mismatch usually points to something in the software path rather than the network itself, and the VPN is the prime remaining suspect — a stuck or misbehaving VPN tunnel can block all traffic even while the phone shows a strong 5G signal.

**Next single step: disconnect the VPN.**

- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Network & Internet**
- Tap **VPN**
- Tap the gear/settings icon next to the connected VPN
- Select **Disconnect**

Once it's disconnected, check that the 🔒 icon is gone from the status bar, then run the speed test again and tell me the result.

Also please let me know: is this a VPN you use regularly (for work, security, or streaming), and does it normally work fine? That'll help me decide whether reconnecting it later makes sense.

If the speed test works with the VPN off — the VPN was the culprit, and you can decide whether to keep it off or try reconnecting it fresh. If it still says "No Connection" even with the VPN off, tell me and we'll move on to the next step — I'd have you **reboot the device** to let everything re-register, and if it's still dead after that, I'll get you transferred to our technical support team since that would point to a line or network issue on our end.

I understand the frustration — you've fixed everything the status bar was flagging and it's still dead. Since the VPN is ruled out, the next step is:

**Reboot your device.**

You've changed several network settings in a row (data toggle, data saver, and the 2G → 5G network mode change). A restart forces the phone to re-register on the network and reload all those settings fresh — it resolves a lot of cases exactly like this where the status bar looks fine but no traffic flows.

- Press and hold the **power button**, then tap **Restart** (or "Reboot")
- Wait for it to fully boot back up

Once it's back on:

1. Check the status bar — confirm you still have 📶 signal, 5G/4G, and 📱 Data Enabled
2. Run the speed test again and tell me the result

If it works — you're all set, and it was just the settings needing a refresh.

If it still says **"No Connection"** — don't worry, I'm not going to send you in circles. At that point everything on the device side has been ruled out (airplane mode, mobile data, data saver, network mode, VPN, and now a reboot), which means this is a line or network-side issue that I can't fix from here. I'll get you transferred to our technical support team with a full summary of everything we've already tried so you don't have to repeat yourself.

Go ahead and reboot, then let me know what you see.

You're absolutely right to be frustrated — you've done every step correctly and the account/device side should be working by now. Let me check a couple of things on your account before I hand you off, so the technical team has a complete picture.

turns.thought: I hear you, and I'm sorry — you've done everything right and it's still broken. Let me check a couple more things from my side before we escalate.

I hear you — you've done every step faithfully and the status bar looks perfect, so this is genuinely puzzling. I checked your account while you were working on this, and everything on our side looks normal:

- **Line 555-123-2002:** Active
- **Contract end date:** 2026-12-31 (not expired)
- **Refueled data:** 2 GB applied and showing on the line
- **Device (Smartphone Pro Max):** Activated

So there's no suspension or account issue blocking you. There's one more device-side setting worth checking before I escalate, and it's a very common hidden cause of exactly this symptom — full signal bars but nothing getting through:

**Next single step: reset your APN settings to default.**

The APN (Access Point Name) is the setting your phone uses to actually reach our data network. If it's incorrect, your phone can show a strong 5G signal but still have no data path — precisely what you're seeing.

- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Network & Internet → Mobile network**
- Tap **Advanced** (you may need to scroll)
- Tap **Access Point Names (APN)**
- Tap the **⋮ menu** (three dots, usually top-right)
- Select **Reset to default**

Then **restart your phone one more time** — the reset won't take effect until you do — and run the speed test again.

If that fixes it, you're back in business. If it still says "No Connection," I'm going to stop putting you through more steps and transfer you to our technical support team with a complete summary of everything you've already tried, so you won't have to repeat any of it.

Give that a try and let me know.
